ocr.notes: Gist right but key errors: image says 'Both of the principals were arrested' (transcript: 'None'), bondsman is W. P. Farrell (not W. T.), surety is Jos. Schnaider (not Scinnalder), and 'at several different places' is dropped.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Tom Allen was arrested at the instance of W. P. Farrell of Covington, Ky., one of the bondsmen whose $3,000 bond Allen forfeited after his 1876 fight with Goss.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Post-Dispatch Monday, February 11, 1884', page 8; item in the fourth column.

facts.fact: After his prize fight with Joe Goss in Kentucky, Allen was arrested and gave $3,000 bond to answer an indictment, with W. P. Farrell and P. C. Murphy as bondsmen; Goss was convicted, paid a $300 fine and served a little time
Allen went to England and let his Kentucky bond be forfeited; his bondsmen's property was sold to pay the State
Allen was arrested in St. Louis on a Kentucky requisition procured by bondsman W. P. Farrell of Covington, Ky., after refusing Farrell's money demand; he said he had already paid each surety $250
Allen gave $2,000 bond with Fred Walters and Jos. Schnaider as sureties and said he would prosecute Farrell for attempted extortion

notes: The article dates the Goss fight September 10, 1876; recorded the fight-related fact as 1876-09. Arrest was 'Saturday evening' before Monday Feb. 11, i.e. Feb. 9, 1884. Article 110 appears to be the follow-up (release by Judge Noonan).
